messages.subject: Database format question
parts:
Hello, I'm preparing the dataset to run a dynamic occupancy model with unmarked and the function colext. I would like to receive recommendations on how formatting the spreadsheet in excel in order to convert it to unmarkedMultFrame. Attached is an example of a format (data are not real) that I guess could work but I am not sure. 

I have about 100 sites sampled in 2013 and 2016, and two covariates (grass height and seed abundance: its food) that may change between years and govern colonization and extinction rates. In 2013 I did not make repeated visits to the sites, but in 2016 I did 3 to 4 visits to each site. 

So, apart from recommendations on spreadsheet format to convert to unmarkedMultFrame, I would really appreciate on comments on how relate colonization and extinction rates with habitat covariates grass height and seed abundance.

Thankyou very much in advanced,

Joaquin Aldabe.

messages.subject: Re: Database format question
parts: Joaquín, With only two primary occasions I would not put much hope on a multi-season design. Dynamic parameters describe biological events that take place in transitions between primary occasions, and with only two primary occasions you're left with only one transition. I would consider first a single season model with a temporal effect on detection. The format looks fine to me, but you need more y columns, right?
